The differential metabolome is anchored to **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** — the top hit with an extraordinary fold-enrichment of 632 and FDR = 0.0 — alongside a broader Reactome "Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives" cluster (fold 187.6, FDR = 0.0). Eight of the twelve input metabolites map to the serine/threonine core, with phosphoserine (C01005) and S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021) appearing in both the KEGG pathway and the serine-branching SMP00721 (3-Phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase deficiency) context, indicating perturbation of the one-carbon folate branch linked to this deficiency model.

**Key drivers.** Phosphoserine (C01005) anchors the serine-synthesis limb and is annotated in "Serine metabolism" (WP4688) and "Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways" (WP2525). L-Threonine (C00188) feeds into glycine via the threonine aldolase reaction, bridging amino-acid catabolism to the one-carbon pool. S-Adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), the product of methyltransferase reactions, connects the methylation economy to this network. KEGG BFS confirms the cysteine–cystathionine axis: L-cysteine (C00097) ↔ L-cystathionine (C02291) through O-acetyl-L-serine (C00065) in three enzymatic steps, placing cysteine downstream of the serine/glycine hub.

**Biological significance.** The convergence on glycine–serine–threonine metabolism suggests disrupted one-carbon folate cycling and cross-linked trans-sulfuration, consistent with conditions ranging from metabolic epilepsies (enriched via WP5355) to disorders of methyl group donation. Niacinamide (C00153) and sulfate (C00059) further imply perturbed NAD⁺ salvage and oxidative cysteine metabolism, respectively. Guanidinoacetic acid (C00581) maps to creatine-biosynthesis pathways, indicating a downstream read-out of altered methylation capacity. The 632-fold enrichment — despite a modest input of 12 metabolites — reflects strong pathway specificity and warrants targeted investigation of serine-biosynthesis enzymes and trans-sulfuration flux in the experimental model.
